text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
-- Insurer GAN posts a 965-million-franc loss for the first half due to real-estate, which may jeopardize plans to sell stake in CIC and could force the state to undertake a heavy recapitalisation.
-- Family-owned pharmacy group Pierre Fabre to separate drug and cosmetics activities, to allow for strategic alliances. Group may seek bourse listing.
-- Industrial production rose strongly this summer, partly due to activity in the automobile sector ahead of the September expiry of a government purchase incentive scheme.
-- Head of Paris commercial court plans to take steps to force companies to publish their accounts in order to bring to light those in a precarious financial position.
-- Havas and Generale des Eaux launch joint bid for SFP state-owned film production firm.
-- Belgian group Albert Frere may have bought a further one percent stake in Compagnie de Suez from UAP, two weeks after acquiring a 2.9 percent stake.
-- General Electric and Pratt & Whitney to sign partnership with Airbus Industries on development of "superjumbo" engine.
-- Retired people demonstrated in France on Tuesday against loss of their purchasing power.

-- Daewoo chairman Soon Hoon Bae says Daewoo to participate in Thomson Multimedia recapitalisation, sees French bid for Thomson Multimedia unlikely, reiterates plans to create jobs and seeks to reassure workers worried about planned takeover.
-- President Jacques Chirac accused Israeli security agents in Jerusalem on Tuesday of being overzealous in protecting him from the crowd.
